body.x: Pokde.Net, a Malaysian IT and hardware outlet, named STM Corporation, GEOBOT and Intellectus Corp. its top three innovative companies at the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards.

The Future Innovation tech eXpo 2026 (FIX 2026) ran from Oct. 21 to Oct. 24 at EXCO in Daegu, featuring future mobility, robotics, and AI and ICT technologies and products. In the Global Media Awards, overseas outlets review technologies and products on the show floor, and each outlet chooses its own top three companies.

Pokde.Net is a technology and digital lifestyle outlet headquartered in Malaysia that publishes news and product reviews on IT hardware, gaming, mobile devices, automobiles and the latest gadgets. It values a product's actual build quality, price competitiveness and on-site compatibility more than simple technology promotion. Mubashar Aftab, the outlet's founder and publisher, attended FIX 2026 as part of the global media press corps.

The three companies Pokde.Net chose work in different fields: auto parts manufacturing, physical AI-based infrastructure safety management and industrial data connectivity. Each offers technology that can address real problems at industrial sites.
STM Draws on 50 Years of Automotive Parts Manufacturing to Support Future Mobility

STM Corporation, led by its CEO, has built up automotive parts manufacturing technology for more than 50 years since its founding in 1972. It develops and supplies precision parts such as wheel bearing seals and encoders, along with lamp and battery parts for automotive electrical systems and rubber parts.

Its flagship wheel bearing seal is a core component that keeps moisture and foreign matter from entering the bearing while the vehicle is driven and keeps internal lubricant from leaking out, supporting stable operation of the bearing. Its encoder products provide signals to wheel speed sensors and other components so the vehicle's control system gets the information it needs. Drawing on its technology in materials, design and manufacturing processes, STM focuses on improving the performance and reliability of automotive parts.

As electric vehicles and autonomous driving advance, vehicle electrical systems and precision control parts matter more. Building on its experience in automotive parts manufacturing, STM supplies products to automakers and parts suppliers in Korea and overseas and keeps refining parts technology that supports the future mobility industry.
GEOBOT Inspects Infrastructure Above and Below Ground With Physical AI and Robots

GEOBOT is a deep tech startup founded on a public technology transfer from the Korea Institute of Geoscience and Mineral Resources (KIGAM). It develops physical AI-based autonomous infrastructure inspection robots and an AI-based digital twin platform. Its core technology combines spatial recognition technology such as LiDAR, vision sensors, GNSS and IMU with ground-penetrating radar (GPR) to survey not only the surface but also underground space and build data.

GEOBOT's solution uses autonomous robots and drones to inspect major infrastructure such as roads, railways, bridges, tunnels and airports, and links the data it collects to geospatial information and digital twins to analyze the condition of facilities. In particular, by surveying the same section repeatedly and comparing and analyzing the data, it is developing technology to detect signs of infrastructure problems such as underground cavities and sinkholes and to track changes over time.

While conventional infrastructure inspection relied on site surveys at a single point in time, combining autonomous robots with AI-based analysis can support preventive safety management and predictive maintenance through repeated data collection and change analysis. GEOBOT integrates above- and below-ground spatial data and connects it with AI analysis, presenting physical AI technology to raise the level of safety management for national infrastructure.
Intellectus Connects Industrial Data With Its Real-Time DDS Middleware int2ConneX

Intellectus Corp., a real-time data middleware company led by its co-CEOs, develops software that reliably collects, transmits and integrates data generated by different industrial equipment and systems. Its core solution, int2ConneX, is real-time middleware based on Data Distribution Service (DDS) that supports smooth data flow among various equipment and systems.

Industrial sites mix equipment that uses different communication protocols and systems, which can make it difficult to integrate data and use it in real time. int2ConneX aims to connect heterogeneous industrial protocols and data and to support real-time data collection, conversion and transmission, improving linkage between systems and operating efficiency. The company lists ultra-low-latency data processing, high throughput and quality of service (QoS) support among its main technical features.

Such data connectivity technology can be used in industries where real-time data processing matters, such as smart factories, robotics, mobility, energy and defense. As AI-based automation expands, the base technology that reliably connects and uses the data generated by equipment and systems matters as much as the performance of individual machines. Intellectus supports AI transformation (AX) and digital transformation (DX) at industrial sites through real-time middleware and edge computing technology.
Components, Geospatial Data and Connectivity for Real Industrial Problems

Pokde.Net's top three span auto parts manufacturing, infrastructure safety management and industrial data integration. STM supplies precision parts that support stable driving and control of automobiles, GEOBOT develops technology that uses autonomous robots and AI to inspect the condition of major infrastructure, and Intellectus provides real-time data infrastructure that connects the varied equipment and systems at industrial sites.

In its FIX 2026 pre-event interview, Pokde.Net stressed that the strength of industrial technology and AI lies in producing results at actual sites, beyond flashy demonstrations. It said that linking data with existing systems is important as manufacturing moves to AI, and that robotics and automation technology also have to account for real adoption costs and operating efficiency.

The selection looks at Korean companies' manufacturing, infrastructure and industrial software technology from a global tech outlet's perspective and widens their contact with overseas markets. Pokde.Net weighs a product's actual quality, on-site compatibility and applicability, and the three companies were introduced from that viewpoint.

Ten overseas media outlets from Europe, the Americas and Asia took part in the FIX 2026 Global Media Awards, including Pokde.Net. Each outlet reviewed the technologies and products of exhibiting companies and chose its own top three. Selected companies gain an opportunity to be publicized through overseas media.

The press corps included Leo Thevenet, editor-in-chief of Le Café du Geek, an IT, lifestyle and global technology outlet; Juan Castromil, editor-in-chief of Clipset, a Spanish mobile and consumer electronics outlet; Eliane Fiolet, editor-in-chief of Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley outlet covering IT and consumer electronics innovation; Davis Kim, reporter at AVING USA, a global technology, business and exhibition outlet; Yoshioka Tomomi, editor-in-chief of Otaku Soken, a Japanese outlet covering subculture and AI, virtual reality and IT convergence technology; Sherri Wang, research editor at DIGITIMES, a global outlet covering semiconductor and ICT supply chains; Võ Hoàng Long, reporter and deputy editor-in-chief of VietnamPlus, a Vietnamese state-run general news portal; Stephanie Chen, editor-in-chief of ChinaByte, a Chinese outlet covering IT, enterprise digital transformation (DX) and AI; Dimpal Bajwa, deputy editor of ET Manufacturing, an Indian outlet covering smart factories, robotics and manufacturing technology; and Mubashar Aftab, founder and publisher of Pokde.Net, a Malaysian outlet covering IT hardware, gaming and mobile technology.

The media partners take part in the FIX 2026 Innovation Awards Media Day and in on-site judging for the BEST OF FIX 2026 Global Media Awards during the show, and plan to report on innovative Korean companies in future industries to audiences around the world.
